title: What If Every Snake on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every snake vanished tonight? Millions of people would cheer, until the rats showed up.
Snakes are both predators and prey. They eat rodents, and hawks and owls eat them.
One adult eastern brown snake may eat about 50 mice a year. Across a farm, that adds up to thousands.
Without snakes, rodent numbers would likely surge, and they'd strip crops and native plants.
That would also raise the risk of rodent-borne diseases like hantavirus and plague.
Snakebites kill an estimated 81,000 to 138,000 people a year, so fewer deaths. But a trade-off nobody could control.
